title: Policy hot-reload leaves per-org burst window gaps causing temporary allowance spikes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Customers observed short-lived bursts of unmetered traffic immediately after policy changes (hot-reloads) for per-org and per-route overrides. Symptoms look like a brief spike in allowed requests that bypass normal debit accounting for 1-3 seconds after the config change. This ticket tracks investigation and fixes to ensure policy reloads do not create transient allowance windows or duplicate burst credits.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create org-level policy with base window=60s, burst=100 tokens; create route override with window=60s, burst=50 tokens.
2) Drive steady traffic to route at a rate near the limit until accumulator stabilizes (observe steady throttles in dashboard).
3) Push a policy change (hot-reload) that tweaks an unrelated field (e.g., route metadata) to trigger policy hot-reload without changing limits.

4) Observe a 1-3s window where requests temporarily continue above the prior metered allowance and per-key debits aren't applied correctly; dashboards show drop in meter increments while request volume stays high.
Notes: does not require route rename or shard failover; stable repro with local integration harness and staging cluster under moderate load.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-19 - Initial triage by Asha: reproduces in staging. Repro script attached to ticket in repo: tools/rate-tests/hot_reload_burst_test.go (internal).

2025-02-21 - Connor: Added extra logs around policy version tags and meter key generation. Observed that meter keys for affected route retain old 'window_start' anchor for up to 2s after policy version bump.

2025-02-24 - Hypothesis: race between policy hot-reload code path and per-key accumulator rotation. When policy metadata updates, policy version is replaced but meter-key derivation can use stale version/anchor during in-flight requests leading to temporary mismatch of accumulator namespace and counts. This yields duplicate logical accumulators (old anchor + new anchor) coexisting briefly, effectively doubling available burst tokens for affected keys.

2025-02-25 - Further logs show: (a) policy-change message acknowledged by control plane, (b) serving nodes fetch new policy but do not atomically invalidate local per-key accumulators, (c) gateway replays a handful of inflight requests with old policy context.
root_cause: Non-atomic policy swap combined with per-key accumulator namespace that encodes policy_version-dependent anchors. During hot-reload, some requests map to old accumulator namespace while subsequent requests map to new namespace; both namespaces can hold remaining burst credit concurrently until old namespace expires, creating a transient effective increase in allowance.
impact_summary: Transient over-allow can let orgs exceed committed limits briefly, resulting in under-charging and potential SLAs/abuse vectors. Seen in staging and at least two production customers (private notes linked). Frequency increases with concurrent policy edits and high QPS routes.
proposed_fix: Option A (preferred): Make policy reloads atomic at serving node by applying new policy and immediately invalidating/merging per-key accumulators for policy-anchored namespaces. Implement an in-memory CAS: swap policy pointer, then run a fast aggregator to merge old accumulator counts into new namespace and zero old entries.

Option B: Decouple accumulator namespace from ephemeral policy-version anchors; derive stable meter keys based on persistent logical route IDs + epoch; then perform explicit invalidation only on epoch rollover. This is lower-risk but requires migration of stored accumulator format across shards.
Planned approach: implement Option A for fast remediation in runtime-1.21, plus follow-up refactor (Option B) for long-term correctness in runtime-1.22.
Add unit/integration tests and a chaos test that runs concurrent policy updates while driving traffic to ensure no allowance spikes.
implementation_notes: Patch will add Policy::version_tag and an atomic swap API on serving nodes. After swap, call AccumulatorManager.invalidate_policy_dependent_namespaces(policy_id, old_tag) which will iterate active keys and merge counts into new namespace.
Prefer lock-free path: do best-effort merge with short-lived lock per-key to avoid pausing hot request paths. If merge fails, fall back to synchronous merge with metrics incremented for ops.
Add telemetry: metric runtime.policy.reloads, runtime.accumulator.merges.success, runtime.accumulator.merges.fail, and alert if merges_fail > 0.1% over 5m.
tests: Unit: accumulator namespace mapping table behavior under concurrent version swap.
Integration: staging cluster hot-reload harness reproducer (tools/rate-tests/hot_reload_burst_test.go).
E2E: run for 6 hours with randomized policy updates and verify no transient over-allow occurrences in aggregated metrics.
Regression: add fuzz test to CI that mutates policy metadata and validates per-key meter increments are monotonic and never drop during reload.
notes: 2025-02-26 - PM call with product and support: flagged as P1 due to customer reports. Support owners: Marina Ortiz and Luis Herrera. Communicated mitigation: reduce frequency of policy pushes and avoid editing policies during traffic peaks.
2025-02-28 - Deployed hotfix branch to staging; saw elimination of 1-3s allowance spikes on staging. Running soak for 48 hours before rolling to canary in prod.
2025-03-02 - Canary rollout started for runtime-1.21 with merge patch; monitoring closely for accumulator-merge fail metrics.
